description.value: Two hundred years of cutting has to arrive somewhere, and it arrives all at once. You become host to a Teratoma and it becomes host to you: you gain a passive regenerative or adaptive trait, settled with the GM the first time you rest after reaching 20th level. In the same breath you stop being ordinary meat — resistance to poison and disease, and immunity to your own Blooms, the table simply stops applying to you. Nobody asked whether you wanted both. The Grafter’s road does not have a fork in it this late; it has an arrival.

cinderfall.incomplete: The resistance-to-poison-and-disease clause matches a real pf2e shape (Resistance type:[...] value:N, confirmed via pf2e-source/packs/pf2e/feats/ancestry/dwarf/level-5/blast-resistance.json), but this card's own text states no numeric value for the resistance -- shipping a Resistance rule element with a guessed or missing value would misrepresent the card, so it is not built. "Immunity to your own Blooms" is unbuildable: Bloom has no rule-element representation to grant immunity against. The GM-negotiated passive trait settled at 20th level is undecided at authoring time -- nothing to encode yet.
